sources.entry: Lidify ⚠ - Music discovery tool that provides recommendations based on selected Lidarr artists, using Spotify or LastFM. MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Lidify is a music discovery tool that recommends artists based on the Lidarr artists you select, using Last.fm (Spotify support was removed per the README).
summary.what_it_does: Lidify takes artists you pick from your Lidarr library and finds similar artists to suggest for discovery. The README says that as of November 2024 Spotify API changes prevent its use, so the app now supports only Last.fm, which requires a Last.fm API key and secret. It can add recommended artists to Lidarr via its API, with options for quality and metadata profile IDs, searching for missing albums on add, and a dry-run mode that skips adding. Settings can be provided as environment variables or configured in the web application. It is run as a Docker container exposing port 5000, with auto-start and a configurable delay at startup.
use_cases: discover new music similar to my Lidarr artists
find recommendations from Last.fm listening data
automatically add recommended artists to Lidarr
preview Lidarr additions with a dry run
schedule music discovery at container startup
how_to_run: Create a docker-compose.yml with the lidify service using image thewicklowwolf/lidify:latest
Set last_fm_api_key, last_fm_api_secret and mode=LastFM in environment
Optionally set lidarr_address and lidarr_api_key or configure them in the app
Run docker-compose up -d and open the web interface on port 5000
notable: Works alongside Lidarr, adding recommended artists to it through its API
Last.fm is the only supported discovery source after Spotify API changes
Dry-run mode to test recommendations without adding artists
Configurable via environment variables or within the web app
caveats: Spotify discovery no longer works due to Spotify API changes as of November 2024; Last.fm is required
Requires a Lidarr instance and a Last.fm API account
Setup is in the README only for Docker Compose; no other install method is described
keywords: discover new music similar to my library
